title: SolveIt: The Thinking Developer's Environment w/Jeremy Howard & Johno Whitaker
summary: Jeremy Howard and Johno Whitaker present SolveIt: small-step, human-driven AI use for learning and lasting code, as an alternative to vibe coding and agents.

assertions.quote: doing this a lot over the last year that it also makes the LLMs much more intelligent and works with us much better

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: He has not seen any which have been built you know through vibe coding

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.

assertions.quote: That's not what happened I haven't actually sped up

verdicts.note: METR found devs believed they were ~20% faster while measured slower; other studies also show self-reports outrunning measured gains.

assertions.quote: relying on tab completion and stuff it's damaging our ability to do high quality work over an extended period of time

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.

assertions.quote: Every time you try to get a language model to fix a mistake you make it more likely to make more mistakes of that kind

verdicts.note: Self-correction research shows LLMs rarely fix errors from bare 'that's wrong' feedback, but concrete external feedback such as test output does help iteration.
3 of 47 sources report repetitive prompt-patch cycles 'without convergence', where developers get stuck re-prompting outputs that fail to fix the issue; restarting is not compared.

assertions.quote: any time an AI shows you a function library or an API you're not very familiar with you should stop

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.

assertions.quote: if you don't have kind of web search or grounding you often end up with outdated versions of the OpenAI API

verdicts.note: Training cutoffs reliably cause stale version and model suggestions; checking against current docs is necessary.

assertions.quote: how easy it is to create your own complete agent framework to do exactly what you want no more and no less

verdicts.note: Owning and understanding your workflow helps you debug it, and many practitioners report framework bloat; but there is no comparative evidence, and frameworks can be a good starting point.

assertions.quote: There is no methodology that works with bad coding

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.

assertions.quote: it's really encouraging her to write the code not to do lots of for you all at once

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.

Using AI to generate code (Copilot plus any tool) lowered comprehension of the resulting code. But the study logged no detail on how AI was used, so it cannot compare explanation-style use with delegation, and it did not measure skill formation.

Using ChatGPT for ideation while coding independently improved accuracy, while direct acceptance only raised speed. This is task performance, though; learning and skill retention were explicitly not measured.
